title: Tiramisu
subtitle: Italian coffee dessert with mascarpone and espresso-soaked sponge fingers
excerpt: Layers of espresso-soaked sponge fingers and a rich mascarpone cream, dusted with cocoa, chilled overnight. The iconic Italian dessert that needs no baking and gets better with time.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tiramisu (from the Italian tira mi su, pick me up or lift me up) is a coffee-flavoured dessert that originated in the Veneto region of north-eastern Italy. The earliest documented recipe is associated with the restaurant Le Beccherie in Treviso in the early 1960s, though several other establishments have made competing claims. The original recipe uses savoiardi (sponge fingers), mascarpone, raw egg yolks, sugar, strong coffee, and Marsala wine or dark rum. In the most common British version, the alcohol is often reduced or swapped for amaretto; the raw egg element is sometimes replaced with whipped cream for food safety reasons, although the egg yolk version has much richer flavour. The key to tiramisu is not over-soaking the sponge fingers: they should absorb the espresso and soften but not collapse. The dessert must be assembled and then chilled for at least 6 hours, and preferably overnight, before serving.

content.text: The mascarpone cream must be whisked carefully: over-beating after adding the mascarpone can make the mixture grainy. Whisk the egg yolks and sugar until very pale and the whisk leaves a trail, then fold in the mascarpone and fold in the whipped cream gently. Dip the sponge fingers briefly, one at a time, in the cooled espresso: a count of one on each side is enough. They should be dampened, not sodden. Serve the tiramisu straight from the dish at the table.

items.preparation: strong and cooled; or 6 tbsp instant coffee dissolved in 300 ml boiling water, cooled

content.text: Stir the amaretto into the cooled espresso. Whisk the egg yolks and caster sugar together in a bowl until very thick and pale, about 4 minutes. Add the mascarpone and fold gently until smooth.
Whip the double cream to soft peaks. Fold into the mascarpone mixture. Whisk the egg whites in a clean bowl to soft peaks. Fold into the mascarpone mixture in two additions.

Dip each sponge finger briefly in the coffee, one count on each side, and arrange in a single layer in a dish approximately 30 x 20 cm. Spread half the mascarpone cream over the top. Add a second layer of dipped sponge fingers. Top with the remaining cream. Smooth the surface.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, and preferably overnight. Dust thickly with cocoa powder through a sieve just before serving.
